subject: AI Assurance & Ops Playbook — RFP clarifications
messages:
From: Cobalt Procurement <procure@cobalt.co>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 24 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: RFP — request for AI assurance / ops playbook and clarifications

Hi Naomi,

Thanks for your timely responses to our RFP. Our procurement and model-risk teams at Cobalt have a few specific follow-ups before we finalize scoring:

1) Can you share an operations-level assurance playbook that maps Redwood's controls to the NIST AI RMF core functions (Govern, Map, Measure, Manage) and indicates evidence we can request?

2) For EU AI Act high-risk deployment considerations, can you confirm which workload categories you treat as "high-risk" by policy and whether you provide model documentation (e.g., SRD / technical documentation) as part of onboarding?

3) Please outline your regression sampling/monitoring approach for model updates — frequency, sampling heuristics, and roll-back criteria.

4) Any materials on incident response for model performance drift / unexpected hallucinations (playbook, contact escalation, post-incident evaluation) would be helpful.

We'd appreciate a draft playbook or artifacts by EOD Monday (2027-06-28) so our review committee can include them in the next meeting. If you'd like a short sync to walk through, propose 30 minutes next week.

Thanks,
Sandra Kim
Senior Procurement Manager
Cobalt Insurance
procure@cobalt.co

--
Note: Attachments allowed; please keep any redlined contract language separate in DocuSign or tracked PDF.

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: RFP — request for AI assurance / ops playbook and clarifications

Hi Sandra — thanks for the clear asks. Looping in Connor (runtime/ops) and Vivek (governance & legal) so we can cover all items.

Short answers up front:
- We attached a draft operational playbook (redwood-assurance-playbook-v1.pdf) that maps controls to NIST AI RMF and includes evidence types and retention points.
- For EU AI Act: we treat PII-handling and regulated finance/health classification workflows as high-risk by policy; we provide a standard "Model Technical Dossier" for onboarding and can extend it for the EU Act on request.
- Regression & monitoring: we run pre-deploy regression sampling on canary traffic and post-deploy drift detection with daily telemetry; draft sampling heuristics included in the CSV. Rollback triggers are threshold-based tied to eval regressions on a curated prompt set and customer-configurable SLOs.
- Incident response: our playbook includes incident tiers, immediate mitigation (fallback to a safer model variant), RCA templates, and SLA timelines for customer notifications.

We'll attach three artifacts to this thread and are happy to run a 30-minute walkthrough. Proposed times: Mon 6/28 10:00-10:30 PT, Tue 6/29 14:00-14:30 PT. Which works for you?

Thanks,

Hi Naomi — appreciate the quick turnaround and the attachments. A couple of clarifying Qs after a quick skim:

- In the NIST mapping spreadsheet, column D lists "evidence examples". Can you confirm whether those artifacts are produced routinely (automatic retention) or only on an ad-hoc request basis? For audit purposes we need to know retention/availability windows.

- For the EU Act: is the Model Technical Dossier generated per-model version, or only at onboarding? Our legal team will need per-version traceability for the deployment variants we label as high-risk.

- On regression sampling: do you support bespoke sampling sets per customer (to mirror in-production distribution) or only a Redwood-curated set? We would prefer a hybrid approach if possible.

Also — Markus (consultant) will be reviewing your playbook; he's been helping us scoping evidence requests. We're aiming to reach a baseline for contract language around "evidence delivery windows" and "incident notification SLA".

If you can confirm the above points and commit a timeline for any per-version artifacts, we'll classify this as "compliant" for our next gate review.

Best,
Sandra

Subject: Re: RFP — request for AI assurance / ops playbook and clarifications

Sandra — quick follow-up with specifics and commitments. See attachments and links. Summary below.

1) Evidence generation & retention: most artifacts in the NIST mapping are produced routinely as part of our platform telemetry and governance workflows (model manifests, audit logs, rollout snapshots). We retain policy-relevant artifacts for a minimum of 180 days by default; extended retention packages are available (12/36 months) under enterprise contracts. Evidence types that are ad-hoc (e.g., manual assessment memos) are flagged in column F of the spreadsheet.

2) Model Technical Dossier cadence: we generate a baseline dossier at onboarding and create a new versioned dossier for any model architecture or weights change that affects outputs. For customer-specific fine-tuning or parameterized runtime variants (e.g., safety-tuned prompts / system messages), we can generate per-version notes on request. Commit: can provide per-version SRD within 10 business days for high-risk variants.

3) Regression sampling approach: Redwood supports hybrid sampling — we provide a Redwood-curated core prompt/eval set plus tooling to ingest customer-supplied production traces to seed sampling. Canary sampling is configurable (percent of traffic, stratified by route/tenant). Rollback: automatic rollback when regression delta exceeds configured threshold on the customer-specified gold set, or manual rollback via ops runbook.

4) Incident response specifics: Playbook includes Triage (T0/T1/T2), Mitigation (automatic fallback to a conservative variant, traffic routing to Dedicated nodes), Communication (initial customer notice within 60 minutes of detection for P1 incidents), and Post-incident reporting (72-hour interim brief, 14-day RCA). Contact matrix included in appendix.

Next steps & timeline:
- We uploaded the latest artifacts to the Drive link (DocSend link also provided).
- Per-version dossiers for any identified high-risk model variants: turnaround 10 business days after request.
- If acceptable, I'll schedule a 30-minute walkthrough for Tue 6/29 14:00 PT.
